verses.7:148: وَٱتَّخَذَ قَوۡمُ مُوسَىٰ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ مِنۡ حُلِيِّهِمۡ عِجۡلࣰ ا جَسَدࣰ ا لَّهُۥ خُوَارٌۚ أَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ أَنَّهُۥ لَا يُكَلِّمُهُمۡ وَلَا يَهۡدِيهِمۡ سَبِيلًاۘ ٱتَّخَذُوهُ وَكَانُواْ ظَٰلِمِينَ
verses.20:88: فَأَخۡرَجَ لَهُمۡ عِجۡلࣰ ا جَسَدࣰ ا لَّهُۥ خُوَارࣱ فَقَالُواْ هَٰذَآ إِلَٰهُكُمۡ وَإِلَٰهُ مُوسَىٰ فَنَسِيَ

meaning: The root خَوِرَ (khawira) has two cores per Ibn Fāris: a sound — خارَ الثورُ, the lowing of an ox — and weakness or softness. From the second come خَوَّار, applied to a coward, a brittle spear, or yielding ground.
en_note: Statistically derived from translation co-occurrence, not a lexical definition. Highlighting only.
meaning_previous: The root خَوَّارٌ (khawwār) primarily denotes weakness, feebleness, or softness, applied to people (cowardly), spears, arrows, or land.
meaning_source: Derived from the classical dictionaries (chiefly Maqayis al-Lugha, Ibn Faris d.1004) held in lexicon_full/
